60-Hz fields can stimulate cutaneous mechanoreceptor units and that this stimulation is probably due to field-induced vibrations of skin.

60-Hz, 600-kV/m electric fields, when applied to the surface of a cat's paw, can stimulate a variety of mechanoreceptors, including rapidly adapting field receptors, rapidly adapting high-frequency units, and type T hair-fiber receptors.
